entities.summary: Hud, also known as Eber, is believed in Islam to have been a messenger sent to ancient Arabia before Muhammad. He is repeatedly mentioned in the Quran, whose eleventh chapter is also named after him. Hud lived in the 5th century CE, during a time of great turmoil and transformation in the Arabian Peninsula. As a prophet, he was tasked with warning his people of the impending disasters and urging them to repent and turn to Allah. Despite his efforts, Hud's people ultimately refused to listen, and he was forced to flee to the mountain of Hudhayr, where he met Muhammad and shared his message of prophecy. This encounter is seen as a pivotal moment in the development of Islam, as it marked the beginning of the Islamic tradition and established the foundation for the Prophet Muhammad's mission. Hud's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his story has been retold and reinterpreted in Islamic texts and art throughout history. His name has become synonymous with prophetic authority and divine guidance, and his message of warning and repentance continues to resonate with Muslims to this day.
